{{ModBox}}
'''Thunderbolt''' is a [[mod]] that gives arrows fired from primary [[:Category:Bow|bows]] a chance of exploding on impact of a surface or an enemy.

==Stats==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
! [[Mod#Mod Rank|Rank]]
! Proc Chance
! [[Mod#Attributes|Cost]]
|-
| 0 || +7.5% || 6
|-
| 1 || +15% || 7
|-
| 2 || +22.5% || 8
|-
| 3 || +30% || 9
|}

==Drop Locations==
{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*The explosion deals 250 {{D|Blast}} damage to the target, as well as to nearby enemies within 10 meters of the blast.
**The explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]].
**Unlike the area blasts of dedicated blast weapons like Launchers, Thunderbolt does NOT have a safety distance to prevent self-stagger. Furthermore, if the shot hits and explodes close enough to you it will do a full Knockdown instead of just a self-stagger.
**The explosive damage from this mod cannot be increased with base damage, such as {{M|Serration}}, and elemental mods such as {{M|Hellfire}}, but it will be increased by Bane mods, like {{M|Bane of Infested}}.
*Compared to Launchers, the Thunderbolt blast has full [[Punch Through]] (like most Launchers) and '''zero''' falloff throughout its entire area of effect (unlike most Launchers), so all enemies take full damage even at the outer-most edges of the blast while behind cover.
*The blast area is increased by {{M|Firestorm}} or {{M|Primed Firestorm}}.
*The explosions are silent.
*Arrows fired at terrain and other surfaces still explode, but not arrows fired at teammates or other allies.
*When the explosion occurs, the projectile of the arrow causing that is actually "dissolved". Thus any subsequent mechanics relating to the projectile will not happen, such as [[punch through|punching through]] or the spore coming after the arrow of {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}.
*Cannot be equipped on {{Weapon|Lenz}}.
*Can be paired with {{M|Cautious Shot}} to reduce stagger effects.
*The explosion will trigger effects that activate upon damaging enemies; for example, the Thunderbolt explosion created from an {{Weapon|Evensong}}'s projectile will apply [[Puncture]] status effects to each enemy it hits.

==Tips==
*As the blast damage is not improved by damage increasing/elemental mods on the corresponding bow but it IS reduced by the resistances/armor of the enemies, viable builds using Thunderbolt rely on sending out a massive number of arrows quickly to have as many explosions as possible.
*Pair with a high-rank [[Multishot]] mod for maximum effect. Calculating per shot, there will be a 48.9% chance of at least one explosion with both {{M|Split Chamber}} and Thunderbolt at max rank. The chance for two explosions is 8.1%. With Split Chamber, {{M|Vigilante Armaments}}, and Thunderbolt there is a 58.4% chance of at least one explosion, a 15.3% chance of at least two explosions, and a 1.4% chance of three explosions.
*When facing groups of enemies at medium-to-long range, maximize splash damage by aiming for a nearby surface rather than directly at an enemy.
*Since explosive damage is unaffected by the amount of time the shot has been charged, rapid shots can be more effective at quickly taking out large groups of enemies.
*This mod pairs well with the {{Weapon|Attica}} or {{Weapon|Zhuge}} due to the high volume of fire of crossbow-type primaries compared to other bows, ensuring a very high chance of bolts exploding within a short period of time. Combined with the higher ammo capacity, using Thunderbolt on these weapons is very effective for dealing with crowds.
**Combining the Attica or Zhuge, especially modded for [[Fire Rate|fire rate]], with {{WF|Mirage}} while using her {{A|Hall of Mirrors}} ability can create an extremely large number of explosions over a wide area, since arrows fired by Mirage's clones can also proc Thunderbolt.
***The {{Weapon|Zhuge Prime}} does not benefit from this mod, as the arrows already have a guaranteed explosion after making contact.

==Patch History==
{{Scrollbox/Article|
{{ver|35}}
*Fixed the Thunderbolt Mod causing self-damage to Ivara when equipped on her Artemis Bow.

{{ver|30.8}}
*The explosion FX for Thunderbolt have been updated.

{{ver|27.2}}
;Self Damage Changes:
We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. 

The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger.

With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe.

{{ver|18.10}}
*Improved the FX and performance of the Thunderbolt mod.
*Reduced the FX of the Thunderbolt mod on Mirage's clones to improve performance.

{{ver|14.2.1|fix}}
*Improved performance of Thunderbolt explosions on low end systems.

{{ver|9.8}}
*Fixed Thunderbolt explosive damage trumping impact damage. Projectile damage now applies first, and then the chance to explode is checked.

{{ver|7.10}}
*Introduced.
}}
{{Ver/Lu|27.2}}

==Acquisition==

{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*Casting an ability will stop the energy generation for '''1''' second.
**Channeled abilities that drain energy over time, such as {{A|Immolation}}, {{A|Sound Quake}}, and {{A|Renewal}} will completely prevent energy generation for as long as they are active and for '''1''' second afterwards. Abilities with variable energy drain such as {{A|Artemis Bow}}, {{A|Pacify & Provoke}} and {{A|Desecrate}} do not interrupt the energy generation.
*All stacks of the buff expire simultaneously at the end of the duration. Applying a new stack refreshes the buff duration.
